AI delivery governance & agentic operating models

AI tools everywhere.
Better delivery?
Harder to tell.

Vitalii Oborskyi · Delivery leader, researcher & author.

I help software organizations investigate why AI adoption is not improving delivery, rebalance review and ownership, and define controls for agentic systems in production.

For enterprise software teams and IT services companies.

Discuss your AI challenge ↗Explore the research ↓

AI is a fundamental shift: an attempt to delegate parts of thinking to machines.

I study what that changes in software delivery and the systems we design. My work draws on more than 20 years across quality engineering, project management, PMO and delivery leadership.

changes.before:
01 / Where I can help

Start with the decision
you need to make.

Delivery / Diagnosis

“We bought AI tools.
Delivery is not improving.”

Assess the delivery flow, review and verification capacity, rework, knowledge dependencies and costs. Investigate the actual constraint.

Possible output: a problem/risk map and prioritized experiments or changes to test.

Architecture / Runtime governance

“The demo works.
Production is hard to control.”

Review delegated judgment, permissions, limits, evaluation evidence, cost ownership, escalation and corrective action.

Possible output: a control/ownership sketch and explicit unresolved release questions.

SDLC / QA / Operating model

“Our process and roles
have not caught up with AI.”

Work through requirements, evaluation, release decisions and human capacity in a focused workshop.

Possible output: draft role and decision boundaries, learning routines and an improvement backlog.

The first conversation determines fit and scope; outputs depend on the agreed engagement. Discuss your AI challenge →

Publication information

Reuse & credits.

Linked publications

The writing index links to the original published articles. Those editions retain their own terms and credits. The index does not reproduce the article text, illustrations, slides or PDFs.

Website material

© 2026 Vitalii Oborskyi. No general reuse license has been granted for this website's original text or design. Please contact me about reuse. Individual publications and repository components may carry their own licenses.

Author portrait

The author supplied the source photograph for this site. The displayed portrait is an AI-assisted background-removal derivative, optimized as a transparent WebP image. It is not claimed to preserve every foreground pixel. No general reuse permission for the photograph is granted here; contact me before using it elsewhere.

Language labels

The website interface is English. Publication-language labels use EN for English and UA for Ukrainian; machine-readable language codes are en and uk. UA in a project name means Uncertainty Architecture. A platform edition is not automatically a translation; unconfirmed talk languages are labelled explicitly.

Display preferences

Auto uses your device's local time: Day from 07:00 until 19:00, Night otherwise. You can choose either theme yourself. Theme and motion preferences are stored locally in your browser; no location request, account or analytics is involved. The decorative spatial background follows native scrolling on each page, and topic choices in Writing. The thematic structures also move gently in a repeating cycle while you read. Motion off freezes both the camera and the structures; your reduced-motion preference overrides a saved On choice. Theme changes only recolor that view. No measurement or scientific simulation is represented. Without JavaScript, your device's light/dark preference and a static geometric background supply the fallback.

Research and acknowledgements

Uncertainty Architecture and The Subprime Code Crisis maintain their own research, evidence and attribution records. The acknowledgements identify UA project advisory roles, specific contributions and public discussions. These relationships do not imply institutional endorsement, certification or adoption by PMI, the University of Waterloo, EPAM or another institution.

Corrections and contact

If you spot an incorrect link, date or attribution, please open an issue or contact me on LinkedIn.
